A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same complex-valued 2D Gaussian holography work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction benchmarks, runtime measurements, ablations, simulations, and optical captures in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds CGH comparisons, amplitude-decomposition experiments, a 1D reconstruction study, and pupil-shift results.

M1.justification: The core Gaussian parameterization, rasterizer, BLASM propagation, and principal losses remain unchanged. v2 Supplementary Sec. 12 additionally reports optimization under pupil-shift supervision, a limited training-objective adaptation demonstrated in Fig. 15; its exact loss is not specified.

E1.justification: The main DIV2K evaluation and existing depth-plane, propagation-distance, and optical-capture coverage remain. v2 adds controlled complex-valued 1D signal reconstruction and an explicitly supervised shifted-pupil scenario, extending beyond the generic pupil-shift illustration already present in both versions.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds NH3D, TensorV2, and GWS to the Smooth POH comparison and Wirtinger holography to Random POH. NH3D also enters the supplementary optical-capture comparisons. These substantially broaden the evaluated CGH comparators; Table 1's representation-method membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The principal 50-image, two-plane evaluation and default training settings remain. v2 adds rendering latency to the CGH comparison, intermediate reduction ratios, and parameter-matched amplitude controls. Table 2 revises U-Net's reported size from 8.4M to 2.2M parameters; this establishes a reporting change, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds the Gabor-versus-pixel budget study, amplitude-decomposition ablation with a matched-parameter control, spatial-alignment visualizations for paired Gaussians, and spectrum/pupil-shift analyses. These investigate representation efficiency, factorization, and viewing robustness beyond v1's existing guidance, Gaussian-count, depth, and propagation-distance analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added space-frequency uncertainty discussion concerns a mathematical property, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Substantial additions include Wirtinger's 25.3 dB result against the retained 29.4 dB for ours, new rendering latencies, 3:1 and 7:1 reduction results, and Table 5's 29.5 versus 30.7 dB amplitude-ablation results. New 1D, pupil-shift, and NH3D capture results also appear. The graffiti example from v1 Fig. 6 is removed, while most matched earlier scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Sec. 3.1 adds Gabor's elementary-signal formula and an argument that Gaussian factorization attains minimum space-frequency uncertainty. This is a limited mathematical characterization without a new formal proof. The existing rasterization and propagation derivations in the appendices are retained.

C1.justification: The headline contribution becomes an adaptation of prior complex-valued 3D Gaussians to hologram optimization. v2 emphasizes 5:1 reduction, relegates 10:1 to an ablation limit, and replaces the 2.5-fold memory claim with approximately 30% savings against autodiff implementations. It emphasizes competitive CGH fidelity rather than broad superiority, demotes noise suppression to a side effect, and adds Gabor-based and 3200-fold rendering claims.

C2.justification: New discussion explains amplitude factorization, spatial alignment, and Gaussian guidance as a structured prior. v2 explicitly limits the default objective to the eyebox center, distinguishes uniform spectra from uniform viewing quality, and acknowledges indirect Random POH conversion. It also expands explanations of the simulation-to-hardware gap. The paired-baseline explanation shifts from real/imaginary components to amplitude/phase, leaving its interpretation ambiguous.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code access reference, identifies the focal-stack generation source and gsplat implementation for the paired baseline, and clarifies whether POH conversion is included in reported training times. The detailed optical setup, optimizer settings, and kernel algorithms were already documented in v1's main text or supplement.

R1.justification: v2 elevates the already-cited complex-valued holographic radiance fields work to the explicit foundation of its contribution. It more sharply distinguishes single-view optimization from 3D novel-view synthesis and eyebox expansion, acknowledges concurrent Gaussian-based double-phase compression, and adds relevant Gabor, Wirtinger, pupil-aware, and artifact-resilient holography literature.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statement, positioning, evaluation discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The former combined future-work/conclusion section becomes separate Discussion and Conclusion sections, and the supplement gains dedicated amplitude-decomposition and eyebox-analysis sections. This exceeds routine language editing or renumbering.

P2.justification: The entire document changes from two-column to single-column layout with extensively rearranged figures, tables, and equations. v2 adds analysis figures and Table 5, expands CGH and paired-Gaussian panels, introduces NH3D capture panels, and removes one representation-comparison scene. Tables gain columns and ranking highlights, while several retained figures are recomposed horizontally.

improvement.justification: Broader CGH comparisons, amplitude controls, code-access information, and clearer novelty and eyebox limits improve evidential support and claim calibration. The gain is tempered by weaknesses in the added material: Fig. 5 does not support Gabor superiority at every budget, pupil-shift supervision is under-specified, and the paired-baseline description and Table 5 parameter budgets remain unclear. Overall, v2 is better supported and more carefully scoped, but these issues limit the net improvement.
